title: Building Your First AI Workflow
description: Turn a repetitive AI task into a reusable, reliable workflow you can run in minutes.

data.text: An AI workflow is a repeatable sequence of prompts and steps that reliably produces the output you need. Building one shifts you from "asking AI random questions" to "using AI as a dependable system that saves you time every week."
Anatomy of an AI workflow

data.caption: Every effective AI workflow has five components — build all five before considering it complete
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  T[1. Trigger\nWhat starts it?]
  I[2. Input prep\nWhat context does AI need?]
  P[3. Prompt chain\nWhat prompts run in sequence?]
  O[4. Output format\nWhat does the result look like?]
  R[5. Review step\nWhat do YOU check?]

  T --> I --> P --> O --> R

  style T fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style I fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37
  style P fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style O fill:#ffe1cc,stroke:#bc4c00
  style R fill:#eddff8,stroke:#8250df

terms.definition: What event starts the workflow? A meeting ending, a new email, a document being uploaded, a weekly schedule.
What context, data, or text does the AI need to work with? Where does it come from? How do you paste or send it?
Two or more prompts that run in sequence — the output of one becomes the input of the next.
What does the final result look like? Bullet list, markdown table, Notion entry, JSON, email? Define this upfront.
The human checkpoint. What do you verify before the output goes anywhere? Every workflow needs at least one.

data.text: Design for reliability from day one

Reliable workflows are designed, tested, and instrumented. Think about failure modes, verification, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints before you automate. Small upfront discipline prevents large downstream operational costs.

rows: Canonicalize inputs (trim, normalize names, map synonyms)
Reduces prompt ambiguity and inconsistent outputs
Add schema validation and confidence thresholds
Prevents malformed data from entering downstream systems
Redact PII and apply least-privilege access
Protects privacy and reduces compliance risk
Log failures and schedule periodic prompt reviews
Keeps workflows accurate as inputs change

data.text: A complete workflow example: meeting notes

data.title: Meeting Notes → Notion workflow
data.content:
1. TRIGGER: Meeting ends, recording transcript is available

2. INPUT PREP: Copy the raw transcript and paste into Claude

3. PROMPT 1 (Summary):
"Here is a meeting transcript. Summarize:
- Key decisions made (with rationale)
- Open questions not resolved
- Action items format: [Owner]: [Task] by [Date]
Keep the entire summary under 300 words."

4. PROMPT 2 (Table):
"Convert the action items into a formatted table with columns: Owner | Task | Due Date | Priority"

5. OUTPUT: Paste both into the Notion meeting page

6. REVIEW: Check that action item owners are correctly identified (AI may mix up names)

data.text: Why prompt chaining works better than one big prompt

Asking AI to do five things at once in a single prompt produces mediocre results across all five. Breaking the task into a chain of focused prompts — where each step gets full attention — produces dramatically better results.

rows: Each step is the full focus of one prompt
Errors in step 1 cascade through everything
You can fix step 1 before moving to step 2
Hard to identify what went wrong
Easy to pinpoint and fix the weak step
One chance to get it right
Iterative — improve each link in the chain

data.text: Add verification and deterministic checks

Verification reduces risk. Use deterministic checks (regex, JSON schema, numeric validation), lookups (database or API), and small code-run steps to confirm critical fields before accepting outputs automatically.

data.caption: Verification step inserted between AI output and final action
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  AI["AI output"] --> V["Verification (schema, lookups, numeric checks)"]
  V -->|pass| Commit["Commit / Publish"]
  V -->|fail| Human["Human review / correction"]
  Human --> Commit

  style AI fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style V fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style Human fill:#eddff8,stroke:#8250df
  style Commit fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37

data.text: Prototype and validate: benchmarks, datasets, and acceptance criteria

Create a small benchmark dataset that reflects real inputs, including edge cases and adversarial examples. Define acceptance thresholds for accuracy, format adherence, latency, and safety. Run the prototype across the benchmark and record failure modes.

rows: Compare model outputs to ground truth on benchmark
Measure end-to-end response time under load

data.text: When to use retrieval (RAG) and memory

If your workflow needs up-to-date facts, company documents, or user-specific context, use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Store canonical documents in a vector DB and retrieve only the most relevant passages to condition the prompt. This keeps prompts short and grounded.

data.caption: RAG pattern: retrieve relevant docs, condition prompt, generate grounded output
data.definition:
graph TD
  Q["User input"] --> R["Retrieve relevant docs (vector DB)"]
  R --> L["LLM conditions prompt on retrieved context"]
  L --> O["Generate grounded output"]

  style Q fill:#fff3bf,stroke:#d97706
  style R fill:#e6f4ff,stroke:#0366d6
  style L fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style O fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37

data.text: When to orchestrate with agents

If your workflow must call multiple tools (search, code execution, calendar, email) and make decisions between steps, consider an agentic orchestration layer. Agents can plan, call tools, and loop until success — but they require stronger guardrails and logging.
Security, privacy, and data handling

Treat data handling as a first-class design requirement. Redact or tokenize PII, use enterprise plans when connecting production data, and apply least-privilege credentials for any tool that can write or take irreversible actions.

rows: Run PII detector before sending text to model
Separate read-only and write keys; require human sign-off
Choose vendor plans that opt out of training
Use private instances or contractual training opt-out

data.text: Monitoring and KPIs for workflows

Instrument workflows with both operational and quality metrics. Operational metrics track system health; quality metrics track correctness and user impact. Use alerts to catch sudden drops in performance or spikes in verification failures.

rows: Investigate recent prompt or data drift
Increase human review or tighten checks
Update prompts or add examples for edge cases

data.text: Versioning, testing, and prompt operations
Treat prompts and workflow definitions like code: version them, run tests, and roll back when needed. Keep a changelog of prompt edits and the benchmark results that motivated each change.

data.caption: PromptOps cycle: edit → test → benchmark → deploy → monitor
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  Edit["Edit prompt / template"] --> Test["Run test suite / benchmark"]
  Test --> Bench["Record benchmark metrics"]
  Bench --> Deploy["Deploy new prompt version"]
  Deploy --> Monitor["Monitor metrics in production"]
  Monitor --> Edit

  style Edit fill:#fff8c5,stroke:#9a6700
  style Test fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da
  style Deploy fill:#d1f3d8,stroke:#1a7f37
  style Monitor fill:#ffe1cc,stroke:#bc4c00

data.text: Copyable templates and prompt snippets

rows: "Input: [transcript]\nTask: Summarize key decisions (3 bullets), list open questions, and extract action items as JSON: [{owner, task, due_date}]."

"Examples:
Input: 'Payment failed' → Output: 'billing'
Input: 'App crashed' → Output: 'technical'
Now classify: [ticket text] → Output:"
"Input: [text]\nExtract: date, company, amount. Output CSV row: date,company,amount"
Keep schema explicit and test with edge cases

data.text: More workflow templates to build

data.title: High-value workflow ideas:
items: Weekly review: paste your task list → AI produces a prioritized plan for the week
Email triage: paste email threads → AI classifies as urgent / FYI / action needed
Job application: paste job description + your CV → AI writes a tailored cover letter first draft
Content brief: paste a topic and audience → AI produces an outline with headings and key points
Research digest: paste 3-5 articles → AI extracts key findings and patterns across them
Decision memo: describe a decision → AI formats pros/cons/risks/recommendation

data.text: Start by documenting a workflow you already do manually. Then identify which steps require language, judgment, or synthesis. Build your AI prompt chain around exactly those steps.

data.title: Build your first workflow
data.description: Choose one of the following templates and build your version this week.
steps: Pick a task you do every week that involves writing, summarizing, or analyzing text
Write down the 3-5 steps of how you currently do it manually
Identify which steps AI can replace (writing, summarizing, formatting)
Write a prompt for each AI step
Test with real data from your actual work
Refine the prompts until you get output you would actually use
data.expectedOutcome: A working prompt chain that saves you 15-30 minutes per week on a recurring task

data.title: Workflow building checklist
points: Define the trigger and final output before writing a single prompt
Break complex tasks into a chain of focused, simpler prompts
Include a human review step — AI workflows need checkpoints
Save your finished workflow as a text template for reuse
Improve one step at a time when the output is not quite right

data.text: Common failure modes and mitigations

rows: Add examples, tighten instructions, or canonicalize inputs
Monitor metrics, refresh examples, retrain or update retrieval
Add verification, cite sources, use deterministic calculators

data.text: Operational readiness checklist

items: Audit logging enabled for all tool calls
